ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AD$ is the angle bisector of $\triangle ABC$, and $AE$ is the altitude of $\triangle ABC$. Given that $\angle B=40^\circ$ and $\angle DAE=15^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle C$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given the construction,\\
$\because AE$ is the altitude of $\triangle ABC$,\\
$\therefore \angle AEB=90^\circ$,\\
$\because \angle B=40^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle BAE=50^\circ$,\\
Also, $\because \angle DAE=15^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle BAD=50^\circ-15^\circ=35^\circ$,\\
$\because AD$ is the bisector of $\triangle ABC$,\\
$\therefore \angle BAD=\angle CAD=35^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle BAC=70^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle C=180^\circ-\angle B-\angle BAC=180^\circ-40^\circ-70^\circ=\boxed{70^\circ}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \textbf{Solution:} Given the construction,\\ $\because AE$ is the altitude of $\triangle ABC$,\\ $\therefore \angle AEB=90^\circ$,\\ $\because \angle B=40^\circ$,\\ $\therefore \angle BAE=50^\circ$,\\ Also, $\because \angle DAE=15^\circ$,\\ $\therefore \angle BAD=50^\circ-15^\circ=35^\circ$,\\ $\because AD$ is the bisector of $\triangle ABC$,\\ $\therefore \angle BAD=\angle CAD=35^\circ$,\\ $\therefore \angle BAC=70^\circ$,\\ $\therefore \angle C=180^\circ-\angle B-\angle BAC=180^\circ-40^\circ-70^\circ=\boxed{70^\circ}$
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, A is above, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, and BC is the horizontal base; D and E are both on BC, and the order is B, D, E, C; from A to D there is drawn line segment AD, from A to E there is drawn line segment AE, and AD is located between AB and AE. Reasoning: The problem statement gives that AE is the altitude of △ABC, so AE⊥BC, therefore △ABE is right-angled at E, and ∠AEB=90°. Also ∠B=40°, so ∠BAE=90°−40°=50°. In the figure AD is between AB and AE, and ∠DAE=15°, therefore ∠BAD=∠BAE−∠DAE=50°−15°=35°. AD is the angle bisector of ∠A, so ∠CAD=∠BAD=35°, thus ∠BAC=70°. Finally in △ABC, ∠C=180°−∠B−∠BAC=180°−40°−70°=70°.
